references.text: The Lord promises to bless bread and water, and to keep sickness away from Israel when they serve Him and keep His commandments.
The command to serve (עבד) the Lord your God alone.
The call to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul.
Blessing over the basket and kneading trough as part of covenant promises.
Sickness from Egypt as punishment for disobedience, in contrast to the promise to remove sickness through obedience.
The Lord who heals (יהוה רֹפְאֶךָ) and the promise to keep Egyptian diseases away through obedience.
The Lord heals all your diseases.
Jesus quotes the command to serve the Lord your God alone.
Promise that food and drink will be given to those who first seek God's kingdom.
God will supply all needs according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
Complementary perspectives on the relationship between service, God's material blessing (bread), and human response.
Mutual illumination of how God's blessing of work creates a foundation for joy in His presence.
Thematic parallel about God's ability to feed His people and protect them as a sign of His presence.
The central role of 'service' as a condition for God's blessing and protection.
Direct thematic expansion: The promise of blessing bread (Exodus) is specified as blessing the storehouse and all work (Deuteronomy).
Theological parallel regarding God's active role as protector who removes harm (sickness/evil) from His people.
